name: Tracking motion and change over time
gist: Following objects through video, predicting how scenes will change, and understanding temporal dynamics in visual data.
explain: A static image freezes the world at one moment. But the real world is dynamic — objects move, scenes change, and understanding video requires reasoning about temporal patterns. Can you follow a person through a crowd across multiple video frames, even when they are occluded by other people? Can you predict how a scene will evolve in the next few frames? Can you understand that a sequence of images tells a story? Tracking and temporal understanding are needed for applications like surveillance (which person is which across frames?), sports analysis (tracking players and the ball), robotics (where did the target go?), and autonomous driving (where will the pedestrian be in two seconds?).

The core difficulty is that motion is ambiguous and objects disappear and reappear. In a single frame, you might identify a person. In the next frame, the camera panned, the lighting changed, and the person is now at a different location and appearance. How do you know it is the same person and not someone new? Simple pixel matching fails because appearance changes so much. You need to reason about motion consistency: objects move smoothly, not teleporting. You need to handle occlusion: an object is hidden behind something but might reappear. You need temporal context: the trajectory so far constrains where an object could go next. Longer-term, predicting the future is even harder: it requires understanding physics, intent, and social interaction.

Researchers tackle temporal understanding through several approaches. Some train models to link detections across frames: given boxes in frame t and frame t+1, decide which boxes are the same object. This matching can use appearance features, motion models that extrapolate trajectories, and graph algorithms that solve for consistent tracks. Others use recurrent neural networks or transformers to process video as a sequence, learning temporal patterns implicitly. Some focus on optical flow — estimating the motion of every pixel between consecutive frames — which provides explicit motion information. Others combine detection and tracking in an end-to-end model that jointly reasons about what objects are present and how they move. A few tackle prediction: train models to generate future frames based on past frames, implicitly learning physics and scene dynamics. The goal is to make machines understand video not as a series of independent snapshots, but as a coherent narrative of change over time.

papers.title: Foreground-Aware Token Routing Vision Transformer for Real-Time Satellite Video Tracking
papers.contribution: Surpasses existing real-time trackers in accuracy while achieving inference efficiency comparable to DCF-based methods.

papers.title: GOT-Edit: Geometry-Aware Generic Object Tracking via Online Model Editing
papers.contribution: GOT-Edit achieves superior robustness and accuracy across GOT benchmarks, particularly under occlusion and clutter.

papers.title: MotionMAR: Multi-scale Auto-Regressive Human Motion Reconstruction from Sparse Observations
papers.contribution: MotionMAR achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on AMASS dataset, providing structure-aware and reliable motion reconstruction from sparse observations.

papers.title: PointRePar : SpatioTemporal Point Relation Parsing for Robust Category-Unified 3D Tracking
papers.contribution: Outperforms category-unified and category-specific SOTA methods across three benchmarks while enabling joint training across multiple categories.

papers.title: TAPTRv3: Spatial and Temporal Context Foster Robust Tracking of Any Point in Long Video
papers.contribution: TAPTRv3 surpasses TAPTRv2 by large margins on challenging datasets and achieves state-of-the-art performance even compared to methods trained on large-scale internal data.

papers.title: Action-Guided Attention for Video Action Anticipation
papers.contribution: Generalizes well from validation to unseen test sets on EPIC-Kitchens-100; post-training analysis reveals action dependencies and counterfactual evidence internalized by the model.

papers.title: BigMaQ: A Big Macaque Motion and Animation Dataset Bridging Image and 3D Pose Representations
papers.contribution: Provides subject-specific textured avatars and a benchmark (BigMaQ500) linking surface-based pose vectors to frames across multiple individuals, advancing beyond sparse keypoint tracking.

papers.title: Decouple and Cache: KV Cache Construction for Streaming Video Understanding
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on Streaming Video QA benchmarks with an average 2.5% accuracy improvement over prior methods, as a training-free mechanism.

papers.title: Let's Split Up: Zero-Shot Classifier Edits for Fine-Grained Video Understanding
papers.contribution: Substantially outperforms vision-language baselines on category splitting while preserving accuracy on the rest of the taxonomy.

papers.title: Mango-GS: Enhancing Spatio-Temporal Consistency in Dynamic Scenes Reconstruction using Multi-Frame Node-Guided 4D Gaussian Splatting
papers.contribution: Mango-GS achieves state-of-the-art quality and fast rendering speed for high-fidelity reconstruction and real-time rendering of dynamic scenes.

papers.title: Open-o3-Video: Grounded Video Reasoning with Explicit Spatio-Temporal Evidence
papers.contribution: Open-o3-Video improves mAM by 14.4% and mLGM by 24.2% over baseline on V-STAR benchmark with grounded reasoning traces supporting confidence-aware test-time scaling.

papers.title: RELO: Reinforcement Learning to Localize for Visual Object Tracking
papers.contribution: 57.5% AUC on LaSOT_ext without template updates; confirms reward-driven localization superior to prior-driven approach.

papers.title: STORM: Segment, Track, and Object Re-Localization from a Single Image
papers.contribution: Improves annotation-free pose tracking and reliably recovers from severe occlusions and viewpoint changes on LM-O and YCB-Video.

papers.title: UniTrack: Differentiable Graph Representation Learning for Multi-Object Tracking
papers.contribution: Demonstrates up to 53% identity switch reduction and 12% IDF1 improvements across challenging benchmarks with 9.7% MOTA gain on SportsMOT via seamless architecture integration.
